notes: mechanism none beside a provider record is the shape this schema version exists for, and it is the common one: this substrate offers no in-instance namespace, so a writing pair against it used to have nowhere to go and refused. It now resolves to a seeded copy. The two records are independent and one entry may carry both, either, or neither — kafka carries the in-instance record and no provider, and a store carrying neither is equally expressible and refuses like any store with no answer.

Deliberately mechanism none, and deliberately carrying no nameForm: nothing here needs a generated name, and recording a form nobody established would be a guess this file exists to show is unnecessary. A store recording neither form is undetermined, which refuses — see references/coordination-identity.md.

Choosing a numeric position inside the instance would isolate the keyspace and NOT pub/sub: a message published on one database reaches a subscriber on another, so channel names collide across every one of them. It is never done here for a second reason too — a position inside a running instance is drawn from a fixed set nothing owns, so two worktrees can take the same one and never find out.
Channel prefixing would be an application change, not an overlay knob. Any service that publishes here is refused unless the risk is accepted explicitly.

Subscribing here is fan-out, not competition: every subscriber receives every message, so an overlay consumer takes nothing from the base stack. It is therefore never recorded in competesOn — the hazard it does carry is duplicate processing.

The competes boolean is what the gate reads; competesOn beside it holds the KNOB, group.id, and the distinct value an overlay would attach under belongs in overlayIdentity. Until one is recorded and verified distinct the pair stays refused.
Its postgres record is the undeclared store classified anyway: dependsOn names only events and kafka, and a store a unit forgot to declare is exactly the one the gate exists to catch.

Its Redis subscription is deliberately absent from competesOn. Pub/sub is fan-out: both subscribers get every message and neither takes delivery from the other, so nothing is stolen. The hazard there is duplicate processing, which lands in this overlay's own index — and would still be refused if that duplicated work sent email, webhooks or payments.

prepareCommand clones the dependency tree instead of reinstalling it: near-instant, near-zero disk, and each server keeps its own pre-bundle cache. The clone flag is platform-specific and this repoRoot is a Linux path, so the command uses GNU cp's --reflink=auto, which clones on btrfs or XFS and falls back to a plain copy elsewhere. The macOS equivalent is cp -Rc, an APFS clone; -c is not a GNU cp flag and fails on Linux.
